pr_title: Preview issues and PRs on the terminal
pr_body:
Closes #108

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98482/72188471-06db6380-33c0-11ea-8735-f9b6c65225a3.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98482/72188543-34c0a800-33c0-11ea-9d87-42f0a25a970f.png)

This PR adds a --preview flag for the `view` command in both `issue` and `pr`. When specified, the
pr/issue is printed to the command line with metadata, coloration, and a link to the pr/issue in the
browser.

:warning: It adds more fields to PR queries (title, body, author, etc) that are not relevant to other PR
queries; this means it might slow down other PR queries by a small factor. It didn't seem wise to
refactor our PR queries right now, but I could see adding `prPreview` api commands that include all
the extra fields. I can do that in a follow up PR if others agree.

## markdown support

This PR adds markdown rendering. I ran into some issues finding a reliable library for this; the first one I tried had some strange behavior and was difficult/impossible to configure. The second one was more flexible but one of its dependencies was pinned to a broken, erroneously released version. Given its MIT license, I inlined the library in order to fix the dependency issue myself. I think we will want to build on it anyway and it's only about ~300 sloc.

issue_context.title: Add flag to `pr view` and `issue view` to view in terminal instead of browser
issue_context.body: Use `gh [pr or issue] view [-t or --text]` to output the title and body
comments: Note for `gh pr create` that `-t`, `--title` is already be used to supply a title. Maybe just `--text`? or use a capital T but I see that getting confusing...
Ah yep good point. I was thinking maybe `-p`, `--preview`? But would love to hear ideas for what makes sense here.
👍 on the preview one. That makes better sense.
